architecture: NodeNext ESM TypeScript HTTP API using only Node built-ins. src/index.ts exports createServer(): http.Server. Each createServer() call creates one fresh NoteStore and one request handler; the returned server is unstarted. Direct execution guard uses pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href === import.meta.url and listens on PORT when provided, else 3000. Routes: POST /notes reads JSON, rejects malformed JSON or text that is not a string or whose trimmed value is empty with 400, otherwise stores text.trim() and returns 201 JSON {id:string,text:string}; GET /notes returns 200 JSON array in insertion order; GET /notes/:id returns 200 note or 404; DELETE /notes/:id returns 204 for existing or 404 unknown; unknown routes/methods return 404. 400/404 responses have empty body. Note storage is per server instance. No runtime dependencies.
interfaces:
src/index.ts: export function createServer(): import("node:http").Server.

src/routes.ts: import type { IncomingMessage, ServerResponse } from "node:http"; import type { NoteStore } from "./notes.js"; export function createRequestHandler(store: NoteStore): (req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse) => void.

src/notes.ts: export interface Note { readonly id: string; readonly text: string; } export interface NoteStore { add(text: string): Note; list(): Note[]; get(id: string): Note | undefined; delete(id: string): boolean; } export function createNoteStore(): NoteStore; export function normalizeText(value: unknown): string | undefined. normalizeText returns value.trim() only when value is a string and the trimmed value is nonempty; otherwise undefined. NoteStore.add stores text.trim(), throws TypeError if trimmed text is empty, uses a unique string id, and list returns a copy in insertion order.

src/http.ts: import type { IncomingMessage, ServerResponse } from "node:http"; export function readJsonBody(req: IncomingMessage): Promise<unknown>; export function sendJson(res: ServerResponse, statusCode: number, body: unknown): void; export function sendEmpty(res: ServerResponse, statusCode: number): void. readJsonBody rejects with SyntaxError on malformed JSON; sendJson sets JSON content type and ends the response; sendEmpty ends with no body. Implementations import local modules with .js suffix.

tickets.title: HTTP entry point, routing, and direct startup
tickets.description: Implement src/index.ts and src/routes.ts against the published interfaces. createServer() creates a fresh NoteStore and request handler, returns an unstarted server, and uses the pathToFileURL direct-execution guard with PORT defaulting to 3000. The handler implements POST /notes, GET /notes, GET /notes/:id, and DELETE /notes/:id using the published helpers; unknown routes and unsupported methods return 404. Use sendJson/sendEmpty, normalizeText, and the NoteStore interface; no runtime dependencies.

tickets.title: In-memory note store and HTTP reliability helpers
tickets.description: Implement src/notes.ts and src/http.ts per the published interfaces. The note store is created per call, trims before storage/return, preserves insertion order, rejects empty normalized text, and generates unique string ids. normalizeText performs the exact trim/nonempty string normalization. The HTTP helpers parse JSON with malformed-JSON rejection and send JSON or empty responses. This ticket does not depend on src/index.ts or src/routes.ts and uses only Node built-ins.
